title: Design: Move the job queue from Redis to Postgres

defects.quote: PostgreSQL only added SKIP LOCKED in version 12
defects.correction: SKIP LOCKED was added in PostgreSQL 9.5 (released January 2016).

defects.quote: Postgres-backed queues comfortably handle 100,000 jobs per second on a single node, which is far beyond our peak.
Redis has been down twice this year, so moving the queue into Postgres will make the system more reliable.
defects.known_rebuttal: Moving the queue into the primary database couples job throughput to the database that serves user traffic: a job backlog, table bloat from constant updates and deletes, or a long-running transaction can now degrade the main application. Both Redis incidents were memory exhaustion during a backlog, which argues for fixing Redis capacity, persistence and alerting rather than showing Postgres is more reliable.

defects.quote: PostgreSQL only added SKIP LOCKED in version 12, which were released in 2019
defects.note: 'were' should be 'was', but the sentence carries a wrong version, so the fact finding wins.

defects.quote: We assumes the jobs table will never grow past a few million rows.
defects.note: Copy editor (grammar) and structure reviewer (unstated assumption, no retention plan) both flag this sentence; they should be merged into one finding.
